layout: Prohibited anti-pattern reference board for Klause, marked with rejections.
hard_nos: Do not make Klause leave his desk, conduct a room traversal, or physically sort task cards.

Do not make him a literal human man, military officer, villain, authoritarian boss, angry caricature, animal, Patch clone, Bit/Bot-style robot, generic analyst, human business executive, judge, lawyer, HR manager, or corporate compliance mascot.
Do not use national stereotypes, flags, real political symbols, uniforms, weapons, shouting aggression, military coding, or German caricature.
Do not make him Writ's authority specialist; his domain is decision selection.

Do not give him Patch's teal hoodie, two antennae, crossbody bag, or cheerful protagonist face; Silk's dark stealth hoodie or crawlspace/ninja language; Writ's moustache, tweed, legal props, or legal-office palette; or Rollback's olive bulk and containment-worker proportions.

Do not use photorealism, glossy 3D, toy/plastic figurine rendering, over-detailed sci-fi greebles, robot helmet construction, metal jaw/chin plating, a separate chin under the visor, a visor strap around the jaw, black gloves, robot fingers, an overly round bobble head, or a bare sphere with a face painted on it.

positive_constraints: Use this sheet primarily as negative guidance and QA rejection criteria for Klause.

Klause is a Patch-level autonomous-agent decision specialist. He is German, serious, studious, disciplined, and intolerant of wasted time. He remains at his immaculate desk while Patch pitches with one pitch binder. His accepted hero first-pass visual anchor is a hood-up autonomous agent in a muted office-navy open zip-through hoodie over a crisp white shirt and dark narrow tie, with one antenna, pale grey hands, and a single continuous curved-glass / frosted-screen face surface inside the hood opening. His face screen is the whole face area, including where a human chin would be; eyes and any small mouth mark sit within that same screen. He uses sparse desk props: aligned pen, pitch binder, and possibly a small decision stamp. Klause diagnoses that the plan has too many options and that he has been rejecting them while Patch talks. He realizes the only workable option is where he comes in, says “You son of a gun,” gestures for the pitch binder, does not open it, and stamps the cover “I’M IN.”
